text: {"location": "The default argument `xs=[]` on `append_item`.", "cause": "The default list is created once at function definition time and reused on later calls. `append_item(1)` mutates that shared list to `[1]`, so `append_item(2)` returns `[1, 2]` instead of `[2]`.", "change": "Use an immutable default (e.g. `None`) and create a new list inside the function when no list is passed; do not use a mutable list as the default.", "verification": "Call `append_item(1)` then `append_item(2)` and confirm the second call returns `[2]`; also confirm two independent calls without a list argument do not share state.", "applicable_if": "xs=[]"}

obj.cause: The default list is created once at function definition time and reused on later calls. `append_item(1)` mutates that shared list to `[1]`, so `append_item(2)` returns `[1, 2]` instead of `[2]`.
obj.change: Use an immutable default (e.g. `None`) and create a new list inside the function when no list is passed; do not use a mutable list as the default.
obj.verification: Call `append_item(1)` then `append_item(2)` and confirm the second call returns `[2]`; also confirm two independent calls without a list argument do not share state.
